items.title: Political violence: How justifications influence voter approval
items.summary: What happens when political violence is presented as a justified response to threat or injustice coming from an out-group? A study by Ursula Daxecker, director at the Max Planck Institute for Politics and Social Science in Göttingen, and Neeraj Prasad of the University of Amsterdam, published in The Journal of Politics, finds that legitimizing violence can increase public approval of both violence and the parties involved in it. Among BJP supporters, the effect went even further: when violence was portrayed as justified, they were less approving of a peaceful response by their own party.

items.title: [Perspectives] Beyond the battlefield: war and global health security

Monitoring groups documented over 600 attacks on health care, resulting in the deaths of hundreds of health-care workers throughout the conflict. Hospitals in eastern Aleppo and other contested regions were reduced to rubble. Surgeons operated in underground rooms illuminated by generators, and ambulances were targeted while transporting patients between sites.

The physician provisionally diagnosed gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and prescribed omeprazole. items.title: 80 ans du Rassemblement démocratique africain (RDA): la radicalité du PDG, section guinéenne du RDA [1/2]
items.summary: Il y a 80 ans, du 18 au 21 octobre 1946, se tenait le congrès de Bamako, au cours duquel naissait le Rassemblement démocratique africain (RDA), le premier grand mouvement politique panafricain et anticolonialiste. En Guinée, une délégation de leaders politiques guinéens a participé au congrès de Bamako. Peu de temps après, ces responsables ont fondé la section guinéenne du RDA, le Parti démocratique de Guinée (PDG), qui a mené le pays à l’indépendance en 1958. Le fils d’un des acteurs majeurs de l’époque, Mamadou Traoré, dit Ray Autra, nous fait le récit de cette histoire.

This is not necessarily a sign of selfishness or self-importance, but a way for us to better understand others.

MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).

items.title: Alton Military Prison Site in Alton, Illinois
items.summary: Alton, Illinois's State Penitentiary officially opened in 1833, making it the first state prison in Illinois. It was used to incarcerate convicted criminals from across the state and later served as a military prison. During the Civil War, the facility became the Alton Military Prison and was used to hold Confederate prisoners of war. More than 11,000 Confederate soldiers were held there before the prison closed. items.title: [Editorial] Rethinking threats to human survival
items.summary: Much health advocacy is driven by single-issue activism. Communities with a common interest—from AIDS to child health, climate to tobacco control—focus intensely on their own domain. And understandably so. Important progress has been made through often courageous direct action. But this sharply competitive approach is, according to a new Lancet Commission on 21st Century Global Threats to Health, dangerously flawed. Indeed, perhaps the most important contribution of this Commission is to move global health beyond the consideration of individual harms.

items.title: [Editorial] Rethinking lived experience
items.summary: The theme of this year's World Mental Health Day, held on Oct 10, is Lived experiences heard: real voices, real change. On its website, WHO states that the voices of people with lived experience should “shape the policies, services and decisions that affect their lives”. While these are laudable aims, they also serve to highlight the complex challenges involved in lived experience engagement and co-production, both within the field of mental health and beyond.

items.title: [Comment] Retatrutide in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes: what have we learned from TRIUMPH-2?
items.summary: It is a general observation that the degree of weight loss obtained with GLP-1 receptor agonists is less in individuals with type 2 diabetes than in people without diabetes and similar BMI. Could this difference be overcome with the new triple agonists with superior weight-lowering effects? The TRIUMPH-2 study by Virginia Bellido and colleagues1 in The Lancet is a double-blind, parallel-group, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial of the effects of retatrutide, a triple agonist (GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon), in people with obesity and type 2 diabetes.

items.title: [Articles] Status, challenges, and future directions of machine learning in the management of epilepsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.summary: Although machine learning shows promise in predicting epilepsy treatment outcomes, the high heterogeneity and bias—particularly in small sample sizes, handling of missing data, and scarcity of studies with external validation—limit its clinical applicability. Future research should focus on larger, diverse datasets and standardised minimum reporting. Prospective trials are needed to evaluate machine learning models in real-world settings.

items.title: [Review] Machine learning prediction for epilepsy treatment selection and prognosis: achievements and challenges
items.summary: Accurate prediction of treatment response and selection of optimal treatments remain challenging in epilepsy management. With no reliable surrogate biomarkers for treatment response, the current process of selecting an antiseizure medication remains largely a trial-and-error approach. Other non-pharmacological treatment options, such as epilepsy surgery, are viable alternatives for patients with drug-resistant epilepsy. Statistical and machine learning techniques have been used to predict seizure outcomes associated with antiseizure medications and epilepsy surgery.

items.title: [Review] Artificial intelligence models for automated and semiautomated analysis and interpretation of clinical electroencephalography

Advances in digital technology and wearables have enabled large-scale EEG recording, generating vast amounts of data that cannot be managed through traditional visual interpretation by experts. Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to augment human expertise and reduce workloads.
